businessType: Regional bank, $8.2B total assets, 45 branches across three states, $850M net interest income, expanding wealth management ($2.1B AUM). Founded 1987, private equity backed (2018). CEO in role 3 years.
stage: Mature company: Net interest margin (NIM) 3.1% (down from 3.4% 18 months ago, -30bps erosion), net income $82M (down 12% YoY from $93M), efficiency ratio 62% (up from 59%), deposit beta rising (customers switching to higher-yield alternatives). ROA 1.0% (below peer median 1.2%), ROAE 9.5% (below peer median 11%).
ownerGoal: Return ROA to 1.2%+ and ROAE to 12%+ within 24 months to support Series B PE transaction (exit opportunity for PE owner).
ownerConstraints: Regulatory constraint: Compliance costs rising due to regulatory expansion (CFPB rules, Community Reinvestment Act, enhanced monitoring). Cannot cut compliance without regulatory risk.
Competitive constraint: Mega-banks offer higher deposit rates (attracting deposits away from regional bank). Tech-forward fintech competitors attracting wealth management and payments customers.
Cost structure: Personnel costs 43% of revenue (high for retail banking). Legacy systems consuming tech budget; modernization requires 3-5 year capex commitment.
Deposit dynamics: Interest rate environment pressure; as Fed rates stay elevated, customers moving deposits to yield-bearing alternatives (MMAs, CDs, direct Treasury exposure).
Market saturation: Regional market mature; growth must come from market share gains (difficult, price-based) or customer wallet expansion (limited in retail banking).
immediateConcern: NIM compression accelerating: down 30bps in 18 months. Model shows further 20-30bps compression if rates stay elevated and deposit mix continues to shift toward rate-sensitive deposits. At current trajectory, NIM could drop to 2.8%, making 1.2% ROA target unachievable without major cost reduction or fee income growth. Must understand whether NIM compression is temporary (rate environment driven) or structural (permanent competitive/market shift), and identify which levers (pricing, deposit mix, cost structure, fee income) offer improvement path.

Competitive: 3 mega-banks nearby offering 4.5%+ on deposits (vs. bank's 3.8%), 5+ fintechs competing in payments/lending, robo-advisors competing in wealth ($500k+ portfolios)
unavailableData: Customer segmentation by profitability and retention: Which customer segments contribute to ROA? Which are declining or at risk?
Deposit pricing elasticity: How sensitive are deposits to rate changes by segment (consumers, businesses, high-net-worth)?
Fee income potential: Which new fee products (advisory, management fees, transactional) could improve revenue without asset growth?
Cost structure deep dive: Where is the efficiency opportunity (branch consolidation? workforce optimization? process automation)?
Competitive win/loss: Which customers are leaving to competitors? Which are being retained and why?
timeHorizon: 24 months (PE exit window; Series B transaction requires clear path to 1.2% ROA)
riskAppetite: MEDIUM (PE owner wants growth but transaction certainty matters; cannot take balance sheet risks)
